answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting. Each identity’s action sequence per epoch is hashed into a behavioural digest, and the protocol checks whether successive digests stay within a similarity band. A sharp discontinuity triggers a river of re-verification queries spanning prior epochs. An ember of doubt remains attached to the identity until consistent history is rebuilt. Sybil clusters flip behaviour when reassigning identities, so each switch forces the attacker to age fresh histories across many epochs, one raven per identity flagged. Cost: linear in epochs times identities.
